_about: Public-domain Christopher Newman Hall (1816-1902), Congregational minister of Surrey Chapel and Christ Church, London, for the Word Hoard: The Christian Philosopher Triumphing over Death (1850), Come to Jesus (1858 printing), Now (1859), Quench not the Spirit (1861), The American War (1862), the sermon on the assassination of Lincoln (1865), Sermons (1868), The Reasonableness and Efficacy of Prayer (1874), The Lord's Prayer: a Practical Meditation (1883), Atonement the Fundamental Fact of Christianity (1893) and his Autobiography (1898), from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 58 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

nhall-christian-philosopher: The Christian philosopher triumphing over death. A narrative of the closing scenes of the life of the late William Gordon. To which is added a memoir of John D. Godman. By Thomas Sewall (Philadelphia, Presbyterian Board of publication, [185)
nhall-quench-not: Quench not the spirit (New York : Robert Carter & Brothers, 1861)
nhall-american-war: The American war. By Newman Hall, LL.D, vol. 2 (New York, A.D.F. Randolph, 1862)
nhall-lincoln: A sermon on the assassination of Abraham Lincoln : preached at Surrey Chapel, London, Sunday, May 14, 1865 (Boston : Bartlett and Halliday, 1865)
nhall-prayer: The reasonableness and efficacy of prayer (Boston : Noyes, Holmes, & Company, 1874)
nhall-lords-prayer: The Lord's prayer : a practical meditation (Edinburgh : T. & T. Clark, 1883)
nhall-atonement: Atonement : the fundamental fact of Christianity ([London] : Religious Tract Society, 1893)
nhall-autobiography: Newman Hall, an autobiography (New York, Thomas Y. Crowell, 1898)

_excluded.nhall-other: Translations of Come to Jesus (Japanese, Icelandic, Gaelic, Cherokee); his father John Vine Hall's autobiography, which he edited; travel books and verse
